Assertions.Description: Open **PowerToys Settings** from the tray context menu and confirm one window opens on **Home**. Invoke Settings again from the tray and from a module's **Open settings** action; confirm the existing single Settings window is focused and navigates to the requested page rather than creating duplicate main windows.

Expand every navigation group and open every visible module page once. Confirm each selection shows the matching page title, the navigation selection follows the page, and `PowerToys.Settings.exe` remains alive without a navigation failure or blank page.

Open General, expand its update-channel card, and confirm the description and Stable/Insider choices render without a navigation exception, blank content, or Settings process exit. This observation does not change the channel or certify channel-selection/policy behavior.
Confirm the navigation label and destination page title both use File Explorer Add-ons, or the matching localized product label, rather than mismatched names.

Freeze the expected new-feature set from the tested build's matching source/release inputs before observing badges. Check Window Hopper, Shortcut Guide and their navigation groups, plus the matching Home and Welcome module entries. For a set declaring Window Hopper new and Shortcut Guide not new, Window Hopper and its Windowing & Layouts group carry NEW while Shortcut Guide does not. Require each surface to match its declared set; do not infer that set from the observed UI or a newer checkout.

On **Home**, switch the Utilities card between **Alphabetical** and **By status**. Confirm exactly one sort choice is checked, card order matches the selection, and the selected order persists after closing every Settings window and reopening.

Switch Quick Access **All apps** between **Alphabetical** and **By status**. Confirm the choices are mutually exclusive, each order is correct, and the selected order is retained after closing and reopening the flyout.

Open a representative module page and record its enabled state, leave Quick Access open on **All apps**, then return Settings to Home and toggle that module from the Utilities card. Reopen the module page and confirm its toggle, Quick Access, general `settings.json`, and the Runner's actual module state all match the new value. Re-enable it and confirm its deterministic action works again without restarting Windows.

Resize Settings from wide to its minimum supported width and back while Home contains enough cards to scroll. Confirm the update/shortcut controls and Utilities card reflow below the main cards, no giant empty scroll region appears, and no card, toggle, or navigation content is horizontally clipped.

Navigate Home with keyboard and a screen reader. Confirm heading navigation reaches the **Home** level-1 heading and each dashboard card level-2 heading, focus order follows the visual order, and every module toggle has an accessible name and state.

From a non-elevated run, click **Restart as administrator**, approve UAC, and confirm Runner and Settings are elevated. Check **Always run as administrator**, restart PowerToys, and confirm it returns elevated. Clear the checkbox, restart through the non-admin path, and confirm both processes return to medium integrity.

In a disposable VM, enable **Run at startup** and **Always run as administrator**, reboot, and confirm PowerToys starts elevated without a UAC prompt. Then clear **Always run as administrator**, reboot again, and confirm PowerToys starts automatically at medium integrity. Restore the original startup and elevation settings.

Record every module's initial state, turn every available module off from Home, restart PowerToys, and confirm every toggle remains off, representative module processes/events/hotkeys are inactive, and the shortcut card empty state reads **No shortcuts to show.** with one period. Turn every module on, restart, confirm every toggle remains on and representative in-process, standalone, and shell-extension modules respond, then restore the recorded initial state.

Enable Quick Access and confirm tray left-click opens the Quick Access flyout while tray right-click shows **Quick access** as the first command and opens the same flyout. Disable Quick Access and confirm tray left-click opens PowerToys Settings instead, the Quick Access shortcut control is disabled, the configured chord no longer opens the flyout, and the tray context-menu **Quick access** command is removed. Re-enable Quick Access and confirm the command and flyout entry points return.

From the Quick Access launch page, invoke a representative launchable module and confirm its expected window/action appears exactly once. Close only the fixture window and confirm the flyout remains reusable.

Keep Settings open on the **Find My Mouse** page and Quick Access on **All apps**, choose **By status**, then disable Find My Mouse from Quick Access. **Without navigating away from or recreating the Mouse Utilities page**, confirm its open-page toggle and Home toggle update immediately, it moves to the disabled group without reopening the flyout, and its launch action disappears or becomes unavailable. Re-enable it and confirm the same existing page, Home, Quick Access, and the module action recover.

Assign Quick Access an unused shortcut and confirm the new chord opens the flyout while the old chord does not. Reopen the shortcut editor, click **Reset**, and confirm Settings does not crash, all shortcut key/modifier fields clear, the chord no longer opens Quick Access, and the cleared state persists after reopening Settings.

Toggle **Show system tray icon** off and confirm the PowerToys icon disappears while Runner remains active and Settings stays usable. Turn it on again and confirm exactly one icon returns and both left-click and right-click actions still work.

Enable **Use theme-aware tray icon**, switch the Windows app theme between Light and Dark, and confirm the icon redraws to remain visible in each theme without restarting PowerToys or creating a duplicate icon. Disable the option and confirm theme changes no longer select the adaptive variant.

Switch PowerToys Settings through Light, Dark, and **Use Windows setting**, reopening Home, General, and What's New after each change. Confirm navigation, cards, dialogs, imagery, text, focus states, and disabled controls remain readable and use one coherent theme at narrow and wide window sizes.

Establish effective Windows Light and PowerToys Dark. Inspect Home, General and What's New at narrow and wide sizes, explicitly including rendered Markdown headings, links, body text and caption buttons in What's New. All must remain readable and follow the selected PowerToys theme, not the opposite Windows theme.

Establish effective Windows Dark and PowerToys Light. Inspect Home, General and What's New at narrow and wide sizes, explicitly including rendered Markdown headings, links, body text and caption buttons in What's New. All must remain readable and follow the selected PowerToys theme, not the opposite Windows theme.

Keep an owned What's New window open with release text rendered and Windows held at Light. Change PowerToys from Light to Dark; the same HWND must remain usable and update its Markdown headings, links, body and caption buttons to readable Dark-theme rendering without a close/reopen workaround.

Keep an owned What's New window open with release text rendered and Windows held at Dark. Change PowerToys from Dark to Light; the same HWND must remain usable and update its Markdown headings, links, body and caption buttons to readable Light-theme rendering without a close/reopen workaround. Restore both original themes after the matrix.

Starting with non-elevated PowerToys, change its language to a different, non-English supported language and click Restart in the language-change prompt. Confirm Settings and Quick Access core chrome, sort labels, and actions use localized resources rather than missing-resource keys or unintended English fallback. Restore the original language through the same language-change flow.

During the localization scenario's actual language-change Restart, record Runner and Settings integrity levels before the action and identify their replacement processes afterward. Both must remain at medium integrity, and General must report that PowerToys is running as the current user. Restart as administrator or tray exit/relaunch cannot substitute for the language-change Restart action.

In the selected non-English language, inspect both Color Picker attribution links. Localize the surrounding wording, preserve Martin Chrzan, Color Picker, Niels Laute and UX, and retain the respective destinations https://github.com/martinchrzan/ColorPicker/ and https://medium.com/@Niels9001/a-fluent-color-meter-for-powertoys-20407ededf0c without missing-resource keys or unintended English attribution fallback.

In the selected non-English language, confirm Image Resizer localizes attribution wording while preserving Brice Lambson and ImageResizer, retaining https://github.com/bricelam/ImageResizer/, and showing no missing-resource key or unintended English attribution fallback.

In the selected non-English language, inspect both Mouse Utilities attribution links. Localize the surrounding wording, preserve Raymond Chen, Find My Mouse, Michael Clayton, Mouse Jump and FancyMouse, and retain the respective destinations https://devblogs.microsoft.com/oldnewthing/author/oldnewthing and https://michael-clayton.com/projects/fancymouse without missing-resource keys or unintended English attribution fallback.

In the selected non-English language, confirm Mouse Without Borders localizes the original-contributors attribution while preserving both supplied forms of Truong Do's name, including the original Vietnamese diacritics. Retain https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/COMMUNITY.md#mouse-without-borders-original-contributors and the separate Mouse without Borders product link http://aka.ms/mm; show no missing-resource key or unintended English attribution fallback.

In the selected non-English language, confirm New+ localizes attribution wording while preserving Christian Gaardmark, New++ and Productivity Plus Pack, retaining https://www.onegreatworld.com/products/productivity-plus-pack/?ref=settings_pt, and showing no missing-resource key or unintended English attribution fallback.

In the selected non-English language, confirm Quick Accent localizes attribution wording while preserving Damien Leroy and PowerAccent, retaining https://github.com/damienleroy/PowerAccent, and showing no missing-resource key or unintended English attribution fallback.

In the selected non-English language, confirm PowerToys Run localizes the Window Walker attribution while preserving Beta Tadele and Window Walker, retaining https://github.com/betsegaw/windowwalker/, and showing no missing-resource key or unintended English attribution fallback. Its separate Wox product name/link https://github.com/Wox-launcher/Wox/ remains unchanged.

In the selected non-English language, confirm Text Extractor localizes attribution wording while preserving Joseph Finney and Text Grab, retaining https://github.com/TheJoeFin/Text-Grab, and showing no missing-resource key or unintended English attribution fallback.

In the selected non-English language, inspect both File Explorer Add-ons attribution links. Localize surrounding wording, preserve Noraa Junker, Pedro Lamas, G-Code, Binary G-Code, STL and QOI, and retain the respective destinations https://noraajunker.ch and https://www.pedrolamas.com without missing-resource keys or unintended English attribution fallback.

In the selected non-English language, confirm PowerRename localizes attribution wording while preserving Chris Davis and SmartRenamer, retaining https://github.com/chrdavis/SmartRename, and showing no missing-resource key or unintended English attribution fallback.

In the selected non-English language, confirm Shortcut Guide localizes attribution wording while preserving Noraa Junker and Shortcut Guide V2, retaining https://noraajunker.ch, and showing no missing-resource key or unintended English attribution fallback.

In the selected non-English language, confirm ZoomIt localizes attribution wording while preserving Sysinternals ZoomIt, Mark Russinovich, Alex Mihaiuc and John Stephens, retaining https://learn.microsoft.com/sysinternals/downloads/zoomit, and showing no missing-resource key or unintended English attribution fallback.

Set one distinctive General value and one distinctive module value, create a Settings backup, then change both values. Restore the backup and confirm both Settings surfaces and their persisted JSON values return to the backed-up state without leaving PowerToys in a partially restored state.

Select a deeply nested backup directory whose full path exceeds the General-page card width. Confirm the path persists, wraps or trims without overlapping adjacent controls, and the complete value is recoverable through text selection or the tooltip before running Backup and Restore successfully from that location.

Trigger **Check for updates**, then inspect both Home and General. Confirm they show the same last-checked value using **Today at ...** or **Yesterday at ...** for recent checks instead of a raw timestamp, and that the value remains correct after reopening Settings.

Before Check for updates, use authorized reversible module toggles to establish a non-default on/off combination and record the full enabled map, persisted General preferences and selected modules' UI/runtime state. Immediately after the actual check and before cleanup, reassert the entire enabled map and all General preferences unchanged, with the selected modules' toggles and actual runtime still matching. Keep timestamp/update-cache changes separate from preferences; final restoration cannot substitute for this immediate observation. Do not download/install or inject a fabricated IPC payload; restore the original fixture state afterward.

On a clean installation or clean user profile with no existing general `settings.json`, open General and confirm **Download updates automatically** is enabled on first render and remains enabled after restarting PowerToys.

In a disposable VM with an older updateable build, record valid root and module JSON settings and start the offered update. Confirm `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\PowerToys\ConfigBackup` contains their pre-update copies. Using an updater fixture that pauses after backup creation but before Runner relaunch, corrupt one designated live JSON file, resume the update, and confirm PowerToys restores that file from the backup, relaunches automatically, reports successful restart, and preserves the other settings.

On a build for which a newer version is available, complete an update check and confirm the tray icon gains one update-available badge while General/Home show the matching available-version state. Confirm opening the update surface does not create duplicate badges and the badge clears after updating to the current version.

Open **What's New** from Home and General, then choose **Open Settings**. Confirm the existing main Settings window returns to **Home**, not a blank or stale module page, and repeated invocation does not create duplicate main windows.

Open What's New or OOBE/SCOOBE, close the main Settings window, and confirm `PowerToys.Settings.exe` remains alive while the secondary window stays functional. Use **Open Settings** to restore the main window, close it again, then close the last secondary window and confirm the Settings process exits cleanly.

Resize What's New and OOBE/SCOOBE wide and narrow. Confirm page content remains within the shared maximum width, PowerToys imagery loads without broken placeholders, release text remains readable, and primary navigation/actions stay reachable without horizontal scrolling.

From Home's shortcut-conflict entry, open the actual conflict window under the configured language without changing any shortcut or Ignore setting. Observe its nonempty native window title and readable visible title at initial usable layout, its populated list or legitimate no-conflicts state, and the surviving Settings process. Close the owned window, reopen through the same entry, and confirm another usable nonempty-titled window. Welcome/What's New results and injected missing-resource branches are not substitutes for this ordinary startup observation.

In an authorized policy fixture, disable Diagnostic data by organization policy and fully close and reopen the fixture's Settings windows. In General's Diagnostics & feedback section, confirm Diagnostic data shows Off, its switch cannot be changed, and This setting is managed by your organization. is displayed. The separate Generate bug report package card's Generate package button must remain enabled. Click once and observe generation progress and successful completion with a newly generated local diagnostic package, without uploading it or submitting a GitHub issue. Restore the original policy and diagnostic-data preference, reopen Settings, and compare the switch value, editability and management notice with the pre-test baseline. Remove only this case's generated package; do not require an originally managed setting to become unmanaged.
